Logix Artemis — base computer is a full desktop built around {processor_id}.

The {expansion_bus_bits}-bit expansion interface supports Plug and Execute. The rear ROM/EEPROM position serves the operating system and the front position serves office/application software. A replaceable, non-hot-swappable video card uses a dedicated keyed connector without consuming a general-purpose slot; buffered data/address, wait/ready and DMA access are provided, but electrical pinout remains open.

Installed RAM must satisfy the selected configuration, and a monitor must connect to a fitted video provider. Cartridges must match both the software platform and their socket role; external application cartridges are supported.

Two matched 32-bit modules form each capacity bank, selected independently on the shared bus. Fill banks in order; decode and refresh every rank. Replace the population when changing density rather than mixing module types. Cross-host connector and timing qualification remains open. The system RAM limit is {maximum_ram_kib} KiB. No parity or ECC is fitted; adding it requires a separately qualified BOM.

Native ERA/AIONix applications use {application_api_id}. They discover usable display dimensions and the native 40 × 25 / 80-column modes through capability queries.

The card uses {graphics_controller_id} and implements {video_link_id} through {display_api_id}. Software selects only modes supported by the controller, monitor profile and available buffer/sprite allocation; unsupported downscaling is rejected.

Display storage is {video_ram_kib} KiB, built from {display_chip_count} {display_chip_id} devices on a {display_bus_bits}-bit bus. Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of this memory. Sprite storage is independent: {sprite_ram_bytes} bytes from {sprite_chip_count} {sprite_chip_id} chips on a separate {sprite_bus_bits}-bit bus.

One shared 2048-byte font; glyph edits affect both pages. Independent font buffering is not advertised in this baseline.

Page selection latches during vertical blank. Double buffering does not guarantee drawing throughput.

Sprite geometry and compositing follow {sprite_protocol_id} {sprite_profile}.

16 KiB with the 128 KiB low-density configuration; 32 KiB with the 256 KiB AION high-density configuration. Expanding a low-density machine does not automatically replace its card.

The Aurelia-derived pixel pipeline contains {pixel_buffer_pages} banks of {pixel_buffer_page_bytes} bytes, holding {pixel_depth_bits}-bit pixels. Separate ownership states prevent the renderer from overwriting a bank being scanned out: {pixel_bank_states}. Completed banks feed output latches and a serializer; the pipeline is prefetched before active display and preserves sync on underrun.

The FIFO sits inside the reused Aurelia controller; it is not another framebuffer.

Two {character_cache_bytes}-byte row caches hold current and next character/attribute rows independently of the pixel FIFO.

Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.

Mono II / Color II use legacy 200-line raster profiles. No 26.88 kHz output and no Mono Pro support. CPU word size does not widen local display memory. All five sprites remain available.

chapters.description:
Logix Artemis PRO — base computer is a full desktop / server built around {processor_id}. The PRO configuration serves as a network server.

The {expansion_bus_bits}-bit expansion interface supports Plug and Execute. The rear ROM/EEPROM position serves the operating system and the front position serves office/application software. A replaceable, non-hot-swappable video card uses a dedicated keyed connector without consuming a general-purpose slot; buffered data/address, wait/ready and DMA access are provided, but electrical pinout remains open.

Installed RAM must satisfy the selected configuration, and a monitor must connect to a fitted video provider. Cartridges must match both the software platform and their socket role; external application cartridges are supported.

Two matched 32-bit modules form each capacity bank, selected independently on the shared bus. Fill banks in order; decode and refresh every rank. Replace the population when changing density rather than mixing module types. Cross-host connector and timing qualification remains open. The system RAM limit is {maximum_ram_kib} KiB. No parity or ECC is fitted; adding it requires a separately qualified BOM.

Qualified AION 64K×1 grades for 256 KB modules: 64/128 chips for the 512 KB/1 MB shipping capacities. The 768 KB target uses paired 128 KB two-rank 16K×1 modules. Shared interface and full-population qualification pending.

Native ERA/AIONix applications use {application_api_id}. They discover usable display dimensions and the native 40 × 25 / 80-column modes through capability queries.

The card uses {graphics_controller_id} and implements {video_link_id} through {display_api_id}. Software selects only modes supported by the controller, monitor profile and available buffer/sprite allocation; unsupported downscaling is rejected.

Display storage is {video_ram_kib} KiB, built from {display_chip_count} {display_chip_id} devices on a {display_bus_bits}-bit bus. Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of this memory. Sprite storage is independent: {sprite_ram_bytes} bytes from {sprite_chip_count} {sprite_chip_id} chips on a separate {sprite_bus_bits}-bit bus.

One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.

Page selection latches during vertical blank. Double buffering does not guarantee drawing throughput.

Sprite geometry and compositing follow {sprite_protocol_id} {sprite_profile}.

The ASIC pixel pipeline contains {pixel_buffer_pages} banks of {pixel_buffer_page_bytes} bytes, holding {pixel_depth_bits}-bit pixels. Separate ownership states prevent the renderer from overwriting a bank being scanned out: {pixel_bank_states}. Completed banks feed output latches and a serializer; the pipeline is prefetched before active display and preserves sync on underrun.

Each bank comprises 40 × 32-bit words and holds 320 pixels, so a 640-pixel line consumes two banks. The renderer expands eight pixels at a time while a separate serializer latch drains ready banks. Underrun blanks pixels and sets a sticky fault.

Two {character_cache_bytes}-byte row caches hold current and next character/attribute rows independently of the pixel FIFO.

The dot clock is {pixel_clock_mhz} MHz. Eight-pixel renderer steps and SRAM latch loads run at {renderer_step_mhz} MHz, rather than requiring one SRAM read per dot. A pixel bank drains in {pixel_bank_drain_us} µs.

Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.

At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

One removable NIC occupies one of the four general-purpose slots, providing server operation over {network_stack_id} and {network_link_id}. Firmware permits {supported_network_rates_kbps} kbit/s, with the highest listed rate as its ceiling. The actual common rate also depends on every admitted station and qualified link.

chapters.description:
Logix Athena — base computer is a desktop/server chassis; mechanical design pending built around {processor_id}.

Its EEPROM BIOS boots and initializes hardware, runs diagnostics and selects ROM-based AIONix2/recovery or disk patches. BIOS capacity and chassis mechanics remain unspecified. External application ROM cards are not supported.

Installed RAM must satisfy the selected configuration, and a monitor must connect to a fitted video provider. The internal system cartridge does not establish support for external application cartridges.

Two matched 32-bit modules form each capacity bank, selected independently on the shared bus. Fill banks in order; decode and refresh every rank. Replace the population when changing density rather than mixing module types. Cross-host connector and timing qualification remains open. Maximum motherboard RAM and socket count remain unspecified and are distinct from the CPU address-space limit.

A replaceable cartridge supplies {system_rom_bytes} bytes of shared executable AIONix2 code; private writable state and patch overlays consume DRAM. Cartridge chip organization, connector, timing and exchange procedure require qualification. {recommended_system_id} preserves documented ERA/AIONix binaries through versioned compatibility, with individual editions still requiring qualification.

The card uses {graphics_controller_id} and implements {video_link_id} through {display_api_id}. Software selects only modes supported by the controller, monitor profile and available buffer/sprite allocation; unsupported downscaling is rejected.

It extends {previous_card_id}; {palette_list_id} adds scanline palette changes.

Display storage is {video_ram_kib} KiB, built from {display_chip_count} {display_chip_id} devices on a {display_bus_bits}-bit bus. Two 16K × 16-bit banks use ordinary DRAM, not dual-port VRAM. Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of this memory. Sprite storage is independent: {sprite_ram_bytes} bytes from {sprite_chip_count} {sprite_chip_id} chips on a separate {sprite_bus_bits}-bit bus.

When palette lists are enabled, reserve 0xFA00–0xFFFF (1536 bytes); text, fonts and framebuffers occupy 0x0000–0xF9FF.

One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.

Page selection latches during vertical blank. Double buffering does not guarantee drawing throughput.

Sprite geometry and compositing follow {sprite_protocol_id} {sprite_profile}.

The ASIC pixel pipeline contains {pixel_buffer_pages} banks of {pixel_buffer_page_bytes} bytes, holding {pixel_depth_bits}-bit pixels. Separate ownership states prevent the renderer from overwriting a bank being scanned out: {pixel_bank_states}. Completed banks feed output latches and a serializer; the pipeline is prefetched before active display and preserves sync on underrun.

Each bank comprises 40 × 32-bit words and holds 320 pixels, so a 640-pixel line consumes two banks. The renderer expands eight pixels at a time while a separate serializer latch drains ready banks. Underrun blanks pixels and sets a sticky fault.

Two {character_cache_bytes}-byte row caches hold current and next character/attribute rows independently of the pixel FIFO.

The dot clock is {pixel_clock_mhz} MHz. Eight-pixel renderer steps and SRAM latch loads run at {renderer_step_mhz} MHz, rather than requiring one SRAM read per dot. A pixel bank drains in {pixel_bank_drain_us} µs.

Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.

Requalify existing renderer/FIFO and 16-bit DRAM organization for 640x400x2 and 640x200x4, refresh, sprite fetches, list prefetch and host/DMA stalls together. No greater upload throughput is promised by added capacity.

All earlier modes and sprite/host/API features retained subject to monitor capabilities. Color Pro 14 and Mono Pro support the 640x400 raster; older displays retain their declared raster limits. Horizontal-retrace palette lists require explicit monitor capability; otherwise use static/vertical-retrace palette updates. No forced high scan rate on old monitors.

implementation_design.arbitration: Independent display-DRAM and sprite-SRAM buses. Display reads and full-array refresh have bounded host/DMA backpressure. Sprite fetches use the separate SRAM bus and existing staging/shifters; completed FIFO banks preserve raster order.
implementation_design.text_fetch: Cache 80 character codes and 80 attributes; prefetch the next row into the second 160-byte cache over eight glyph scanlines. Expand each glyph byte to eight 4-bit pixels; prefetch sprite rows and apply fixed priority before publishing pixels.
implementation_design.line_repeat: Re-fetch repeated bitmap lines; FIFO capacity is not an additional framebuffer or guaranteed retained scanline. Validate 320x100x4 bandwidth and refresh at the selected DRAM grade.

clock_targets.scope: 14.31818 MHz short scanout/counter path; renderer uses block expansion and clock enables, not a full CPU at pixel rate. Process-corner qualification required.

manufacturing_planning.process: 3–3.5 micron NMOS; laser-written process-matched masks from secret facility; wafer fabrication at AION Labs.

chapters.description:
This dedicated graphics ASIC produces {pixel_bits}-bit pixel indices. It performs fetch/address generation, eight-pixel glyph expansion, colour selection and fixed-priority sprite composition; it is not a general-purpose CPU. A separately clock-enabled raster sequencer consumes completed pixels and generates sync.

External display RAM is {display_ram_kib} KiB from {display_chip_count} {display_chip_id} chips. Two {sprite_chip_id} devices form a separate 1 KiB, 8-bit sprite bank. Auto-increment uploads arbitrate against sprite reads; descriptor-bank selection latches at vertical blank. Display reads and full-array refresh impose bounded host/DMA backpressure.

The on-chip storage budget is {internal_storage_bytes} bytes, included in die estimates: two 160-byte character/attribute row caches, 40-byte sprite shifters, 40-byte sprite staging and a four-bank, 160-byte pixel FIFO. Each 40-byte FIFO bank holds 4-bit pixels and moves through {fifo_states}; publish complete banks only, backpressure a full queue and prefill before active display. Underrun emits border colour, maintains sync and records diagnostic status.

The text engine caches eighty character codes and attributes and prefetches the next row over eight glyph scanlines. It expands each glyph byte into eight pixels, fetches sprite rows and applies priority before publishing. Repeated bitmap lines are fetched again: the FIFO is neither an extra framebuffer nor a guaranteed retained scanline.

The master and high-resolution pixel clock target {master_clock_mhz} MHz; low-resolution scanout targets {low_resolution_clock_mhz} MHz. The maximum FIFO output target is {fifo_output_mbytes_s} Mbytes/s. Only short scanout/counter paths operate at dot rate; renderer work uses block expansion and clock enables.

At the 375 ns DRAM-cycle target, eighty glyph reads plus twenty amortized next-row bytes give one hundred display reads and 37.5 µs per scanline on average. Forty sprite bytes take 10 µs on their independent bus at a 250 ns SRAM cycle. The full FIFO holds 320 pixels and drains in 22.349 µs at high resolution; two ready pages allow 11.175 µs. Row transitions, descriptors, refresh, repeated bitmap lines and uploads still require deadline analysis and process-corner qualification; these averages are not a timing proof.

The manufacturing plan uses 3–3.5 µm NMOS, process-matched laser-written masks from the secret facility and AION Labs wafer fabrication. Estimated transistor count is {transistor_range}, with {central_transistor_count} as the central value. At 3 µm, die area is estimated at {die_area_3um_range_mm2} mm², central {die_area_3um_central_mm2}; at 3.5 µm it is {die_area_3_5um_range_mm2} mm², central {die_area_3_5um_central_mm2}.

Display DRAM, sprite SRAM, cable drivers/transceivers and monitor palette/DAC circuitry remain external. The larger sprite-interface package and PCB allowance belongs to assembly cost, not additional on-chip storage.

The controller implements {video_link_id} through {display_api_id}. Software selects only modes supported by the controller, monitor profile and available buffer/sprite allocation; unsupported downscaling is rejected.

The corresponding board is {card_id}; external RAM populations below describe that board rather than memory integrated on the die. The controller has a planning die area of {die_area_mm2} mm², not a measured production die.

Display storage is {video_ram_kib} KiB, built from {display_chip_count} {display_chip_id} devices on a {display_bus_bits}-bit bus. Text/font and bitmap allocations are alternative uses of this memory. Sprite storage is independent: {sprite_ram_bytes} bytes from {sprite_chip_count} {sprite_chip_id} chips on a separate {sprite_bus_bits}-bit bus.

One shared 256-glyph bank per mode. Font allocation 2048 bytes at 8×8, 4096 at 8×16 or 8×10 (16-byte glyph stride). Font writes affect both pages.

Page selection latches during vertical blank. Double buffering does not guarantee drawing throughput.

The ASIC pixel pipeline contains {pixel_buffer_pages} banks of {pixel_buffer_page_bytes} bytes, holding {pixel_depth_bits}-bit pixels. Separate ownership states prevent the renderer from overwriting a bank being scanned out: {pixel_bank_states}. Completed banks feed output latches and a serializer; the pipeline is prefetched before active display and preserves sync on underrun.

Each bank comprises 40 × 32-bit words and holds 320 pixels, so a 640-pixel line consumes two banks. The renderer expands eight pixels at a time while a separate serializer latch drains ready banks. Underrun blanks pixels and sets a sticky fault.

Two {character_cache_bytes}-byte row caches hold current and next character/attribute rows independently of the pixel FIFO.

The dot clock is {pixel_clock_mhz} MHz. Eight-pixel renderer steps and SRAM latch loads run at {renderer_step_mhz} MHz, rather than requiring one SRAM read per dot. A pixel bank drains in {pixel_bank_drain_us} µs.

Card-local sequencer arbitrates display fetch and deadline-reserved independent DRAM refresh before bounded host/DMA transfers with READY. Sprite SRAM has its own 8-bit bus. System DMA/MMU remain dedicated host components; the card does not replace system-memory refresh.

At 250 ns conservative DRAM cycle, 80 glyph fetches consume 20 microseconds per active line; 160-byte row prefetch amortizes across 8/10/16 scanlines. Two row caches and 16-bit reads cover text-row transitions. Verify sprites, refresh and bounded host/DMA slots together at voltage/temperature corners; no guaranteed maximum CPU upload rate.

Read capability descriptor before enabling sync. Mono Pro accepts only raster_640_400; integer-scale legacy modes. Old monitors retain their advertised 200-line raster(s), never 640×400. Native 400-line modes require Mono Pro; new 200-line bitmap modes also work on capable older displays. This is display-mode/API compatibility, not Z80 binary compatibility.

Up to {sprite_count} sprites can appear on each scanline. Each is {sprite_size} pixels at {sprite_bits_per_pixel} bits per pixel, with index {transparent_index} transparent. Lower sprite numbers take priority over higher ones, and all overlay text or background. Signed 16-bit logical coordinates scale with the background and clip at screen edges.

Five patterns occupy 640 bytes. Two banks of 8-byte descriptors use 80 live bytes within a 128-byte reservation, leaving 48 bytes of padding and 256 bytes of scratch space in sprite SRAM.
